gaps.wanted: The QFX5240 line datasheet, which covers the QFX5241. Its address redirects to an HPE document server that refused every request made for this change. Nothing here is the datasheet's; the figures are the guide's.

The depth and the registry size of the OSFP cage. The library's std/osfp has no registry entry and carries an estimated depth; the 23.1 by 13.5 mm opening it uses was measured on another maker's 2RU box and the photograph here agrees with it to 0.3 mm in width.

The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures 20 to 23 carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis; the fan module's "40 mm x 56 mm" does not say which side is the depth.

The speed of the two small cages. The guide's callout 2 and Table 3 say "SFP28 ports" with speeds of 10 Gbps, and the photograph prints 25G between them. They are modelled as sfp28 at 25g, as printed.
The lamp of each SFP28 port. The guide's Table 14 gives each of the two ports one status lamp; neither the photograph nor the guide's flat figures show where it is.

The power of the AC switch. The guide's Power System text says 543 W typical and 1394 W maximum and its Table 15 says 537 W and 1381 W, which the text gives to the DC-with-ORv3 build. The text's figures are used.

The ORv3 switch-tray assembly QFX5241-32OD-DO-T1 and its spare QFX5241-32OD-TCHAS: 21.14 x 1.74 x 31.71 in (Table 10), drawn only in isometric (figures 13 and 14), a different envelope from this device. Its DC supply QFX5241-1U-PWR-DO is therefore not a component here. Not modelled.

The lamps of the management jack. Guide figure 19 and Table 13 describe two lamps on the management port; the photograph shows them at the corners of the jack. The jack is drawn with the library's lamped jack.
The rating label of each supply and the serial number labels (the Locate the Serial Number section). Not drawn.
The two-hole protective earthing terminal, "on the side of the chassis" (guide figure 9, isometric). No flat view of the side is held; the side views are empty.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kit's contract. The guide names QFX5241-1U-4PRMK and no kit contract exists in the library; none is written here.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

chassis.note: guide Table 10, QFX5241-32OD-AO: 1.72 in (4.37 cm) high, 17.26 in (43.84 cm) wide, 23.19 in (58.9 cm) deep and 31.65 lb (14.36 kg) fully loaded without optics. The inch figures are used: 43.7 x 438.4 x 589.0 mm, 1 U.

colour.note: The front plate samples #767b86 (a 4 by 24 px bare patch left of the USB port) and the rear panel #6c6d73 (a 6 by 60 px strip at the left end). The chassis colour is the front's. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The photograph is followed for what is printed. It prints "25G" between the two SFP28 ports; the guide's callouts and Table 3 say SFP28 ports "with speeds of 10 Gbps". The group is stated at sfp28 and 25g, as printed. The guide's text puts the earthing terminal "on the side of the chassis" and "through the left-front mounting bracket"; no earthing pad is on the rear photograph, so none is drawn.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide names the rack mount kit QFX5241-1U-4PRMK (a four-post tool-less kit, Table 4 and the installation chapter). The library holds no contract for it and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 438.4 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-green-tab.note: The green tab at the foot of the management panel, 17.0 mm wide and 2.6 mm tall, is the chassis serial number pull-out (guide figure 15 callout 5, "Pull tab"). It is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models.

gate-1.note: The front photograph's body, between the left and right edges, is 1805 px wide (x 153.7 to 1959 px) and 178.6 px from the top edge to the bottom lip (y 187.1 to 365.7 px), an aspect of 10.1 against 438.4 / 43.7 = 10.03 (0.8 percent out). Scale 4.118 px/mm across, used on both axes with the origin at the left edge and the top edge. The rear photograph's body is 1842 px wide (x 119.6 to 1961 px) and 182.7 px high (y 244.3 to 427 px), 4.202 px/mm across, an aspect of 10.08 (0.5 percent out). Edges were found by thresholding the photographs against their white backdrop and checked in 3.5 to 5 times crops; the soft shadow under each body is excluded.

lifecycle.note: The guide, published 2026-10-11, states no end-of-life announcement and none was found. The device states none announced. Estimated, because absence in the documents is not a notice from the maker.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed in a plate at the upper right of the face, above the model name QFX5241-32OD. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text.

mgmt-panel.note: Right of the last group, from the top: the model name under the maker's logo, the SFP28 pair side by side with their legends below, a vertical USB Type-C port with the SS symbol under it, the RJ-45 management jack (MGMT) and the RJ-45 console jack (CONSOLE) side by side, and under them a strip with the reset button (RESET) and the legends ID, SYS and ALM above three unlit lamps, and a green serial-number tab at the foot (guide figure 15 callouts 1 to 7). There is no time-of-day port and no clock connector on this model. Positions are from the 5 times crop of the photograph at 4.118 px/mm and estimated to 0.4 mm. The ID, SYS and ALM lamps are too dark in the photograph to place within the strip, so each is placed under its legend.

modules.note: The seven fan modules (QFX5241-1U-FAN-O) and the two power supplies (QFX5241-1U-PWR-AO) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component (guide Tables 6 to 8), both new. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Each supply carries its own small fan inside.

port-lamps.note: Each network port has a single RGB lamp (guide, Network Port LEDs, Table 11, figure 16 callout 1). In the photograph two round dots 1.3 mm across stand in the slotted band along the top edge above each column, 4.0 mm apart, at 10.3 and 14.3 mm from the column's left edge and 1.3 mm from the top edge; figure 16 draws them in the same place. They are drawn at 2.0 mm, the library's lamp, 2.05 mm either side of the cage's centre (the photograph's pair stands 0.6 mm right of it, inside the reading error), and which dot is which port is not stated; the left one is taken for the upper port, as the QFX5240 siblings' pairs are. The lamps are unlit. The SFP28 ports show no lamp in the photograph although the guide's Table 14 describes one each.

port-numbering.note: Printed once under each column, on the strip below the lower row, read off the photograph: "N up-arrow down-arrow N+1" with N even, so a column holds ports 2c (upper) and 2c+1 (lower). The SFP pair prints "32 up-arrow 25G up-arrow 33", drawn with "32" and "33" centred on their cages and the arrows 2.2 mm out, up to 0.7 mm from where the photograph prints them, so that no legend is almost centred on its cage. The guide numbers the network ports 0 to 31 and the SFP28 ports 32 and 33. Interface names are not printed and none is stated in the guide, so they are not recorded.

ports.note: Front photograph: 32 OSFP openings, two rows of sixteen, in four groups of four columns. The openings abut on a 23.4 mm pitch inside a group (1348 px of the 3.5 times crop for four columns, 93.5 mm a group) and the groups stand on a 96.65 mm pitch, 3.1 mm apart. The first opening starts at 7.2 mm and the last ends at 390.2 mm (measured) against 390.45 mm computed from these figures. The library's OSFP cage is 23.1 mm wide, so a cage is placed on each column's start and a 0.3 mm gap is left between neighbours. The two SFP cages stand to the right of the last group, side by side, 14.4 mm wide and 9.7 mm tall, from 393.9 and 408.3 mm (callout 2).

power.note: Guide, Power System: "typical power consumption ... is 543 W and the maximum power consumption is 1394 W" for the AC switch; Table 15 prints a maximum of 1381 W and a typical 537 W for the same switch, and the text gives 537 W and 1381 W to the DC-with-ORv3 build. The AC text's 543 W and 1394 W are used. Supply: Table 6, 2400 W from 200 to 240 VAC at 15 A and 1000 W from 100 to 127 VAC at 12 A; the switch is redundant only on the high range.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.202 px/mm, checked against the guide's figure 20: a supply at each end of the one row, PSU0 at the left and PSU1 at the right, and seven fan modules numbered 0 to 6 from the left between them on a 45.3 mm pitch. The fan plates measure 40.5 mm wide and 40.2 mm high; the supplies 55.3 by 40.0 mm (PSU0) and 54.1 by 39.2 mm (PSU1), drawn at the mean, 54.7 by 39.6 mm. A fan symbol, an arrow and the module number are printed at the left of each fan opening, and PSU0 and PSU1 with an arrow beside each supply. The two supplies face the same way, the inlet at the right and the handle at the left of each, in the photograph and in the guide's figure 20. The guide's figure 21 (DC FRU panel) draws the DC-with-ORv3 build, which is not modelled.

row-pitch.note: The upper row's openings start 3.7 mm and the lower row's 19.4 mm from the top edge, 15.7 mm apart, each 13.5 mm tall (13.0 mm for the lower row measured, the shadow under it). A thin bright bar stands between the rows.

sources.note: QFX5241-32OD Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-10-11, 199 pages (Hewlett Packard Enterprise, for Juniper Networks), from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/qfx5241-32od/qfx5241-32od.pdf: the front and rear figures 11 to 14, the port panel figures 15 to 19 and Tables 11 to 14 (lamps), Tables 3 to 9 (variants, power and cooling), Table 10 (physical specifications) and figures 20 to 23 (the FRU panels and the supply). Juniper's studio photographs of the 32OD, front and rear (qfx5241-32od-front-high.jpg, 2100 x 546 px, and qfx5241-32od-rear-high.jpg, 2100 x 641 px, from juniper.net's image library). The documents and the photographs are the maker's and public; the guide carries a copyright notice and no terms of use beyond it, and the image library page carries none, so only facts are transcribed. The QFX5240 line datasheet, which covers the QFX5241, could not be fetched: its address redirects to an HPE document server that refused every request made for this change, so no figure here is the datasheet's. No Visio stencil, 3D model or mechanical drawing is held for the QFX5241. The guide's figures 11 to 14 are line-drawn isometric views; figures 15, 16, 20 and 21 are flat drawings, used to count and read, and the photographs to measure.

usb-port.note: The USB port is a Type-C receptacle, stood on its end (an oval 3.7 mm wide and 9.1 mm tall), with the SS symbol under it. The guide's callout 3 says "USB 3.0 port (SS)" and its Table 3 "1 Type-C USB 3.0 port", so the two agree and the library's USB-C receptacle is turned 90 degrees.

variants.note: Guide Table 4 and Table 5: QFX5241-32OD-AO (AC, airflow out) and the spare QFX5241-32OD-CHAS, "Spare chassis without PSUs and fans". Both share this front panel and the rear bays, so each is a configuration of this device. NOT MODELLED: the ORv3 build QFX5241-32OD-DO-T1 with its DC supply QFX5241-1U-PWR-DO, and its spare QFX5241-32OD-TCHAS. They are the same switch in a 1 OU Open Rack V3 switch-tray assembly, 21.14 x 1.74 x 31.71 in and 21.5 kg (Table 10), a different envelope that a configuration cannot state, drawn in the guide only in isometric (figures 13 and 14) and by the flat DC FRU panel of figure 21, with no 19 in DC build on the guide's list.

vents.note: Rectangular slots in the sheet: a band along the bottom from the left to the status strip, a column at the left edge, a column at the right edge and a field above the SFP pair. The band along the top edge, which the lamps stand in, is not drawn as decor, because the lamp holes lie in it. Drawn as vent decor in the other positions, pitched to the photograph and estimated.
